title: Numbers & Arithmetic
description: Number sets, fractions, arithmetic laws and intervals.
html:
🔢 Numbers & Arithmetic

1. Number sets

$$\mathbb{N} \subset \mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{R}$$

  • $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$ – natural numbers ($\mathbb{N}_0$ including zero)
  • $\mathbb{Z} = \{\dots, -1, 0, 1, \dots\}$ – integers
  • $\mathbb{Q} = \left\{\frac{p}{q} \mid p \in \mathbb{Z}, q \in \mathbb{N}\right\}$ – fractions, decimal expansion terminates or repeats
  • $\mathbb{R}$ – all points of the number line, including irrational numbers like $\sqrt{2}$, $\pi$, $e$

2. Arithmetic laws

Basic laws

$$\begin{aligned} a + b &= b + a, \quad ab = ba \\ (a + b) + c &= a + (b + c), \quad (ab)c = a(bc) \\ a(b + c) &= ab + ac \end{aligned}$$

Order of operations

Brackets → powers → multiplication/division → addition/subtraction.

$$-3^2 = -9, \qquad (-3)^2 = 9$$

Signs

Equal signs → $+$, different signs → $-$. A minus in front of a bracket flips every sign:

$$-(a - b + c) = -a + b - c$$

Division by zero

$\frac{a}{0}$ is undefined. Before dividing by a term, check whether it can be $0$.

3. Fractions

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{a}{b} &= \frac{ak}{bk} \quad (k \neq 0) \\ \frac{a}{b} + \frac{c}{d} &= \frac{ad + bc}{bd} \\ \frac{a}{b} \cdot \frac{c}{d} &= \frac{ac}{bd} \\ \frac{a}{b} : \frac{c}{d} &= \frac{a}{b} \cdot \frac{d}{c} \end{aligned}$$

Example

$$\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{6} + \frac{2}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$$

Typical mistakes

  • $\frac{3 + x}{3 + y} \neq \frac{x}{y}$ – never cancel summands
  • $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} \neq \frac{2}{5}$ – denominators are not added

Compound fractions

Multiply by the common denominator of all inner denominators:

$$\frac{1 + \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{4}} = \frac{4 + 2}{3 - 1} = 3$$

4. gcd and lcm

Via prime factorisation: gcd = common primes with the smaller exponent, lcm = all primes with the larger exponent.

$$60 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5,\quad 84 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7 \;\Rightarrow\; \gcd = 12,\ \operatorname{lcm} = 420$$

The least common denominator is the lcm of the denominators. Also $\gcd(a,b) \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(a,b) = a \cdot b$.

5. Intervals and notation

$$\begin{aligned} [a, b] &= \{x \mid a \le x \le b\} \\ (a, b) &= \{x \mid a < x < b\} \\ [a, \infty) &= \{x \mid x \ge a\} \end{aligned}$$

Scientific notation: $0.000\,052 = 5.2 \cdot 10^{-5}$. When multiplying, exponents are added.
